The library behind each, and what it costs a program:

[cols="1,2,1,2,3",options="header"]
|===
|Backend |Library |Licence |Its own API, reachable |Allocation

|BearSSL
|BearSSL, upstream commit 7bea48e5 and one fix of webcpp's, commit 32381d6e of the mirror webcpporg/bearssl's branch webcpp, built from source
|MIT
|`+<bearssl.h>+`, all of it
|none: the key schedule and GCM's state live inside the object

|OpenSSL
|OpenSSL 3.5.9's libcrypto, built from source and static
|Apache-2.0
|`+<openssl/*.h>+`
|`+from_key+` allocates the cipher's context through OpenSSL's own allocator, outside the program's resource, unless a native program sets `+WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE+`, which sends every allocation of OpenSSL's in the process to `+openssl_memory_resource()+`; a message allocates nothing after `+from_key+`

|ctaes
|ctaes as Bitcoin Core v31.1 ships it (`+src/crypto/ctaes+`), built from source
|MIT
|`+<ctaes.h>+`: `+AES128_init+`, `+AES128_encrypt+` and `+AES128_decrypt+`, the same for 192 and 256, on whole blocks
|none: the key schedule lives inside the object

|libsecp256k1
|libsecp256k1 v0.8.0, built from source with every module on
|MIT
|`+<secp256k1.h>+` and its modules
|`+keypair::from_secret+` allocates the signing context, once, in the `+std::pmr::memory_resource+` it is given; nothing else allocates

|libsodium
|libsodium 1.0.22, built from source
|ISC
|`+<sodium.h>+`, all of it
|none: libsodium's operations allocate nothing on the heap, password hashing and its guarded allocator apart, which crypto does not call (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/internals#branches[libsodium's documentation, internals: branches]); a box, a key pair and an AEAD hold their keys inside the object

|the system's generator
|getentropy on Linux, macOS and WASI; BCryptGenRandom on Windows; crypto.getRandomValues through Emscripten
|the platform's
|none
|none

|no backend
|webcpp's own header-only code
|BSL-1.0
|none
|none
|===

libsodium's own test suite runs in webcpp::hash's own lane `+c-suites+`, `+libs/hash/test/c_suites/Jamfile+`, on every target, against the same `+/third_party//sodium+` that crypto links: `+sign+`, `+box+`, `+box2+`, `+box7+`, `+box8+`, `+box_easy+`, `+box_easy2+`, `+box_seal+`, `+secretbox+`, `+secretbox2+`, `+secretbox7+`, `+secretbox8+`, `+secretbox_easy+`, `+secretbox_easy2+`, `+xchacha20+`, `+aead_chacha20poly1305+`, `+aead_chacha20poly13052+`, `+aead_xchacha20poly1305+`, `+kx+`, `+scalarmult+`, `+ed25519_convert+`, `+codecs+`.
